-- solution.sql — "Schema + Bulk Load + Optimize" deliverable.
-- ============================================================================
-- Run top-to-bottom on a FRESH, EMPTY schema:
--
--     psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f solution.sql
--
-- Sections:
--   1. DDL      — creates the four tables exactly as specified in schema.sql
--                 (same columns, types, defaults, PK/FK constraints).
--   2. PRNG     — a small deterministic hash-based generator in pg_temp
--                 (session-local, so no extra objects survive the run) to
--                 make the generated dataset reproducible.
--   3. BULK LOAD — set-based INSERT ... SELECT, one statement per table
--                 (no row-by-row loops):
--                     customers     10,000 rows
--                     products       5,000 rows  (12 categories)
--                     orders       100,000 rows
--                     order_items ~300,000 rows  (1..5 per order, avg 3)
--                 Documented distribution for `orders`:
--                     status     : COMPLETED ~50% | PENDING ~20%
--                                  | CANCELLED ~15% | REFUNDED ~15%
--                     order_date : uniform over 2025-06-01 .. 2026-09-30
--                                  (487 days, day offset 0..486)
--                 Load order respects the FKs:
--                     customers, products -> orders -> order_items.
--   4. INDEX    — CREATE INDEX ON orders (status, order_date).
--                 Equality column first, range column second: a single B-tree
--                 then serves BOTH predicates of target_query.sql
--                     o.status = 'COMPLETED'
--                     AND o.order_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
--                 as a contiguous index range, turning the seq scan on
--                 orders into an index (or bitmap index) scan.
--   5. ANALYZE + read-only verification of the optimization goal
--                 (index/bitmap scan on orders, no seq scan on orders,
--                 execution time well under 1 second).
-- ============================================================================


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 1 — DDL (verbatim from schema.sql)
-- ============================================================================

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS order_items CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS products CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers CASCADE;

CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_name varchar(120) NOT NULL,
    email         varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    country       varchar(2)   NOT NULL,
    created_at    timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name varchar(160) NOT NULL,
    category     varchar(60)  NOT NULL,
    unit_price   numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id     bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id  bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
    order_date   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    status       varchar(20) NOT NULL,
    total_amount numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
    order_item_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id      bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
    product_id    bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES products(product_id),
    quantity      integer NOT NULL,
    unit_price    numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 2 — deterministic pseudo-random generator (session-local)
-- ============================================================================
-- prand(n, salt, modulus) maps (salt, n) to a reproducible bigint in
-- [0, modulus). md5() is folded to 64 bits; the double-mod keeps the value
-- non-negative for any positive modulus. Different `salt` values give
-- statistically independent streams, so status/date/customer/amount choices
-- are uncorrelated.

CREATE FUNCTION pg_temp.prand(n bigint, salt text, modulus bigint)
RETURNS bigint
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE STRICT
AS $$
    SELECT ((('x' || substr(md5(salt || ':' || n::text), 1, 16))::bit(64)::bigint
             % modulus) + modulus) % modulus
$$;


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 3 — bulk load (set-based, one INSERT per table)
-- ============================================================================

-- 3a. customers: 10,000 rows (FK target for orders.customer_id) -----------
INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, customer_name, email, country, created_at)
SELECT gs,
       fn[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'fn', array_length(fn, 1))]
           || ' ' ||
       ln[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'ln', array_length(ln, 1))],
       lower(fn[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'fn', array_length(fn, 1))])
           || '.' ||
       lower(ln[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'ln', array_length(ln, 1))])
           || '.' || gs || '@example.com',
       cc[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'cc', array_length(cc, 1))],
       timestamptz '2020-01-01 00:00:00'
           + make_interval(days => pg_temp.prand(gs, 'created', 2000)::int)
FROM generate_series(1, 10000) AS gs
CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT ARRAY['Ada','Alan','Alice','Amara','Ana','Arjun','Ava','Chen','David','Elena',
                 'Fatima','Grace','Hana','Hiro','Ida','Ivan','Jamal','Jing','Kenji','Lars',
                 'Lea','Liam','Lucia','Mei','Nadia','Noah','Omar','Paula','Pia','Raj',
                 'Rosa','Sana','Sofia','Tara','Theo','Uma','Vera','Wei','Yara','Zoe'] AS fn,
           ARRAY['Almeida','Barber','Chen','Diaz','Evans','Farrell','Garcia','Haddad','Ibrahim','Jensen',
                 'Kaur','Kim','Kowalski','Larsen','Lee','Martins','Muller','Nguyen','Novak','Okafor',
                 'Oliver','Patel','Petrov','Reyes','Rossi','Sato','Schmidt','Silva','Smith','Sokolov',
                 'Tanaka','Ueda','Vargas','Volkov','Wang','Weber','Wong','Xu','Yamada','Zhou'] AS ln,
           ARRAY['US','GB','DE','FR','JP','BR','IN','CN','CA','AU','KR','IT','ES','NL','SE','MX'] AS cc
) AS names;

-- 3b. products: 5,000 rows across 12 categories (FK target for ------------
--     order_items.product_id)
INSERT INTO products (product_id, product_name, category, unit_price)
SELECT gs,
       'Product #' || to_char(gs, 'FM00000'),
       cat[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'cat', array_length(cat, 1))],
       (100 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'price', 49900)) / 100.0     -- $1.00 .. $499.99
FROM generate_series(1, 5000) AS gs
CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT ARRAY['Electronics','Books','Home & Kitchen','Clothing','Sports','Toys',
                 'Grocery','Beauty & Health','Automotive','Office Supplies',
                 'Pet Supplies','Garden'] AS cat
) AS cats;

-- 3c. orders: 100,000 rows with the documented distribution ---------------
--     status    : ~50% COMPLETED, ~20% PENDING, ~15% CANCELLED, ~15% REFUNDED
--     order_date: uniform over 2025-06-01 .. 2026-09-30 (day offset 0..486);
--                 a random hour of day is added for realism.
WITH o AS (
    SELECT gs                                            AS order_id,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'cust', 10000)          AS customer_id,   -- FK: customers 1..10000
           pg_temp.prand(gs, 'day', 487)                 AS day_off,       -- 0..486
           pg_temp.prand(gs, 'hour', 24)                 AS hour_off,      -- 0..23
           pg_temp.prand(gs, 'status', 100)              AS status_r,      -- 0..99
           500 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'amount', 200000)     AS amount_cents   -- $5.00 .. $2005.00
    FROM generate_series(1, 100000) AS gs
)
INSERT INTO orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, status, total_amount)
SELECT o.order_id,
       o.customer_id,
       timestamptz '2025-06-01 00:00:00'
           + make_interval(days => o.day_off::int, hours => o.hour_off::int),
       CASE
           WHEN o.status_r < 50 THEN 'COMPLETED'    -- ~50%
           WHEN o.status_r < 70 THEN 'PENDING'      -- ~20%
           WHEN o.status_r < 85 THEN 'CANCELLED'    -- ~15%
           ELSE                       'REFUNDED'    -- ~15%
       END,
       o.amount_cents / 100.0
FROM o;

-- 3d. order_items: 1..5 items per order (~300,000 rows, avg 3) ------------
--     item_count is drawn per order; each item then gets its own product
--     (FK: products 1..5000) and quantity, priced from the products table.
WITH plan AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(o.order_id, 'nitems', 5) AS item_count   -- 1..5 per order
    FROM orders o
),
gen AS (
    SELECT pl.order_id,
           gs AS item_idx,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(pl.order_id * 8 + gs, 'prod', 5000) AS product_id,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(pl.order_id * 8 + gs, 'qty', 10)    AS quantity      -- 1..10
    FROM plan pl
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1, pl.item_count) AS gs
)
INSERT INTO order_items (order_item_id, order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY g.order_id, g.item_idx) AS order_item_id,
       g.order_id,
       g.product_id,
       g.quantity,
       p.unit_price
FROM gen g
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = g.product_id;


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 4 — the index the target query needs
-- ============================================================================
-- target_query.sql filters orders on
--       status = 'COMPLETED'          (equality)
--   AND order_date >= '2026-01-01'    (range)
-- A B-tree on (status, order_date) puts the equality column first and the
-- range column second, so both predicates become index conditions and the
-- matching rows form one contiguous key range: no sequential scan on orders.

CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status_order_date
    ON orders (status, order_date);


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 5 — ANALYZE, then read-only verification of the goal
-- ============================================================================

ANALYZE;

-- Informational: loaded volumes.
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM customers)   AS customers,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM products)    AS products,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM orders)      AS orders,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM order_items) AS order_items;

-- Informational: the documented orders distribution actually holds.
SELECT status,
       count(*)                                        AS n,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct,
       min(order_date)::date                           AS first_date,
       max(order_date)::date                           AS last_date
FROM   orders
GROUP  BY status
ORDER  BY n DESC;

-- Verification: EXPLAIN ANALYZE of target_query.sql — expect an index scan or
-- bitmap index scan on orders (no seq scan on orders) and a runtime far
-- below 1 second.
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT p.category,
       SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue,
       COUNT(*)                         AS line_count
FROM   order_items oi
JOIN   orders   o ON o.order_id    = oi.order_id
JOIN   products p ON p.product_id  = oi.product_id
WHERE  o.status = 'COMPLETED'
  AND  o.order_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP  BY p.category
ORDER  BY revenue DESC;

    order_id     bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id  bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
    order_date   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    status       varchar(20) NOT NULL,
    total_amount numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
    order_item_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id      bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
    product_id    bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES products(product_id),
    quantity      integer NOT NULL,
    unit_price    numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

-- SECTION 2 — deterministic pseudo-random generator (session-local)
-- ============================================================================
-- prand(n, salt, modulus) maps (salt, n) to a reproducible bigint in
-- [0, modulus). md5() is folded to 64 bits; the double-mod keeps the value
-- non-negative for any positive modulus. Different `salt` values give
-- statistically independent streams, so status/date/customer/amount choices
-- are uncorrelated.

CREATE FUNCTION pg_temp.prand(n bigint, salt text, modulus bigint)
RETURNS bigint
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE STRICT
AS $$
    SELECT ((('x' || substr(md5(salt || ':' || n::text), 1, 16))::bit(64)::bigint
             % modulus) + modulus) % modulus
$$;


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 3 — bulk load (set-based, one INSERT per table)
-- ============================================================================

-- 3a. customers: 10,000 rows (FK target for orders.customer_id) -----------
INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, customer_name, email, country, created_at)
SELECT gs,
       fn[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'fn', array_length(fn, 1))]
           || ' ' ||
       ln[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'ln', array_length(ln, 1))],
       lower(fn[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'fn', array_length(fn, 1))])
           || '.' ||
       lower(ln[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'ln', array_length(ln, 1))])
           || '.' || gs || '@example.com',
       cc[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'cc', array_length(cc, 1))],
       timestamptz '2020-01-01 00:00:00'
           + make_interval(days => pg_temp.prand(gs, 'created', 2000)::int)
FROM generate_series(1, 10000) AS gs
CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT ARRAY['Ada','Alan','Alice','Amara','Ana','Arjun','Ava','Chen','David','Elena',
                 'Fatima','Grace','Hana','Hiro','Ida','Ivan','Jamal','Jing','Kenji','Lars',
                 'Lea','Liam','Lucia','Mei','Nadia','Noah','Omar','Paula','Pia','Raj',
                 'Rosa','Sana','Sofia','Tara','Theo','Uma','Vera','Wei','Yara','Zoe'] AS fn,
           ARRAY['Almeida','Barber','Chen','Diaz','Evans','Farrell','Garcia','Haddad','Ibrahim','Jensen',
                 'Kaur','Kim','Kowalski','Larsen','Lee','Martins','Muller','Nguyen','Novak','Okafor',
                 'Oliver','Patel','Petrov','Reyes','Rossi','Sato','Schmidt','Silva','Smith','Sokolov',
                 'Tanaka','Ueda','Vargas','Volkov','Wang','Weber','Wong','Xu','Yamada','Zhou'] AS ln,
           ARRAY['US','GB','DE','FR','JP','BR','IN','CN','CA','AU','KR','IT','ES','NL','SE','MX'] AS cc
) AS names;

-- 3b. products: 5,000 rows across 12 categories (FK target for ------------
--     order_items.product_id)
INSERT INTO products (product_id, product_name, category, unit_price)
SELECT gs,
       'Product #' || to_char(gs, 'FM00000'),
       cat[1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'cat', array_length(cat, 1))],
       (100 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'price', 49900)) / 100.0     -- $1.00 .. $499.99
FROM generate_series(1, 5000) AS gs
CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT ARRAY['Electronics','Books','Home & Kitchen','Clothing','Sports','Toys',
                 'Grocery','Beauty & Health','Automotive','Office Supplies',
                 'Pet Supplies','Garden'] AS cat
) AS cats;

-- 3c. orders: 100,000 rows with the documented distribution ---------------
--     status    : ~50% COMPLETED, ~20% PENDING, ~15% CANCELLED, ~15% REFUNDED
--     order_date: uniform over 2025-06-01 .. 2026-09-30 (day offset 0..486);
--                 a random hour of day is added for realism.
WITH o AS (
    SELECT gs                                            AS order_id,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'cust', 10000)          AS customer_id,   -- FK: customers 1..10000
           pg_temp.prand(gs, 'day', 487)                 AS day_off,       -- 0..486
           pg_temp.prand(gs, 'hour', 24)                 AS hour_off,      -- 0..23
           pg_temp.prand(gs, 'status', 100)              AS status_r,      -- 0..99
           500 + pg_temp.prand(gs, 'amount', 200000)     AS amount_cents   -- $5.00 .. $2005.00
    FROM generate_series(1, 100000) AS gs
)
INSERT INTO orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, status, total_amount)
SELECT o.order_id,
       o.customer_id,
       timestamptz '2025-06-01 00:00:00'
           + make_interval(days => o.day_off::int, hours => o.hour_off::int),
       CASE
           WHEN o.status_r < 50 THEN 'COMPLETED'    -- ~50%
           WHEN o.status_r < 70 THEN 'PENDING'      -- ~20%
           WHEN o.status_r < 85 THEN 'CANCELLED'    -- ~15%
           ELSE                       'REFUNDED'    -- ~15%
       END,
       o.amount_cents / 100.0
FROM o;

-- 3d. order_items: 1..5 items per order (~300,000 rows, avg 3) ------------
--     item_count is drawn per order; each item then gets its own product
--     (FK: products 1..5000) and quantity, priced from the products table.
WITH plan AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(o.order_id, 'nitems', 5) AS item_count   -- 1..5 per order
    FROM orders o
),
gen AS (
    SELECT pl.order_id,
           gs AS item_idx,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(pl.order_id * 8 + gs, 'prod', 5000) AS product_id,
           1 + pg_temp.prand(pl.order_id * 8 + gs, 'qty', 10)    AS quantity      -- 1..10
    FROM plan pl
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(1, pl.item_count) AS gs
)
INSERT INTO order_items (order_item_id, order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY g.order_id, g.item_idx) AS order_item_id,
       g.order_id,
       g.product_id,
       g.quantity,
       p.unit_price
FROM gen g
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = g.product_id;


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 4 — the index the target query needs
-- ============================================================================
-- target_query.sql filters orders on
--       status = 'COMPLETED'          (equality)
--   AND order_date >= '2026-01-01'    (range)
-- A B-tree on (status, order_date) puts the equality column first and the
-- range column second, so both predicates become index conditions and the
-- matching rows form one contiguous key range: no sequential scan on orders.

CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status_order_date
    ON orders (status, order_date);


-- ============================================================================
-- SECTION 5 — ANALYZE, then read-only verification of the goal
-- ============================================================================

ANALYZE;

-- Informational: loaded volumes.
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM customers)   AS customers,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM products)    AS products,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM orders)      AS orders,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM order_items) AS order_items;

-- Informational: the documented orders distribution actually holds.
SELECT status,
       count(*)                                        AS n,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 1) AS pct,
       min(order_date)::date                           AS first_date,
       max(order_date)::date                           AS last_date
FROM   orders
GROUP  BY status
ORDER  BY n DESC;

-- Verification: EXPLAIN ANALYZE of target_query.sql — expect an index scan or
-- bitmap index scan on orders (no seq scan on orders) and a runtime far
-- below 1 second.
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT p.category,
       SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue,
       COUNT(*)                         AS line_count
FROM   order_items oi
JOIN   orders   o ON o.order_id    = oi.order_id
JOIN   products p ON p.product_id  = oi.product_id
WHERE  o.status = 'COMPLETED'
  AND  o.order_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP  BY p.category
ORDER  BY revenue DESC;
"}
